bull.b: The Anthropic lease materially improves revenue visibility by converting planned AI capacity into a long-duration contractual commitment. Its scale can support infrastructure investment, deepen customer relationships, and reduce reliance on purely opportunistic bitcoin-mining revenue over the next several years.

Rapid growth in HPC lease revenue indicates that TeraWulf is building a second, more contracted infrastructure business alongside bitcoin mining. Increasing revenue contribution from leasing could improve business mix, support recurring cash generation, and make future growth less dependent on cryptocurrency rewards.

The large liquidity position and Abernathy proceeds provide funding for committed construction and strategic expansion without an immediate need to return to equity markets, according to management. Capital recycling also allows TeraWulf to concentrate resources on larger, directly controlled infrastructure assets.

bear.b: TeraWulf’s strong gross margins have not translated into sustainable operating or net profits, with losses overwhelming gross profit and Q2 also affected by a large warrant revaluation. Continued unprofitability can weaken retained capital and make the business more dependent on financing and asset monetization.

bear.t: Heavy cash burn and weak self-funding
bear.b: Negative operating cash flow shows that the core business has not yet consistently funded itself, while very large negative free cash flow reflects substantial ongoing investment and cash requirements. This creates continuing dependence on liquidity, financing, or asset sales to support expansion commitments.

bear.t: Strained capitalization and high debt burden
bear.b: The reported capitalization leaves limited equity support relative to debt and reduces financial flexibility if project costs, operating losses, or financing needs increase. A thin equity base can constrain capital allocation, amplify balance-sheet volatility, and raise the importance of maintaining access to project funding.
